names: 22nd Street Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement
distance_note: The existing 22nd St Caltrain station (Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St, Dogpatch) sits roughly 400-450m from both Pier 70's and Potrero Power Station's tracked boundaries -- grouped here under Pier 70 as the closer, better-established Dogpatch association.
summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. Design is under way: SFCTA approved $1.3 million for the design phase in April 2026, Caltrain expects to complete design by summer 2027, and SFCTA's April 2026 post said Caltrain was then seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029. In September 2026 the Federal Transit Administration announced a $14.1 million All Stations Accessibility Program award to Caltrain's board for the station (Trains.com, September 16, 2026). Sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

milestones.text: Caltrain and SFCTA begin pursuing federal funding for the station's accessibility project.

SFCTA's Transportation Authority Board packet recommends $1,300,000 in Prop L funds for the project's design phase, part of a total funding plan of $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The packet could not be re-read in October 2026 (it refuses automated fetches); the $1,300,000 design request is confirmed by SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post, the total and breakdown are not re-checked.

SFCTA Board formally approves the $1,300,000 Prop L design-phase allocation (one of three projects sharing a combined $9.8M Prop L allocation that day, alongside the Powell St Improvement and the Mission Bay Ferry Landing).

The Federal Transit Administration announces an All Stations Accessibility Program award of $14.1 million to the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board for ADA improvements at the 22nd Street station (an announced date, not a grant agreement or construction start): Trains.com, published September 16, 2026, says the agency announced the awards "last week". Railway Supply (September 12, 2026) says the FTA published its selection list on September 10 and Progressive Railroading is dated September 11; the FTA's own announcement was not read. The amount is close to the funding gap SFCTA's April 2026 plan had left as "Planned TBD".
Design (PS&E, Plans/Specifications/Estimate) targeted complete; Caltrain expects to complete the design phase by summer 2027 (SFCTA, April 28, 2026).

Target: Caltrain aims to implement the project by June 2029 (SFCTA, April 28, 2026). Construction was not yet funded then; the FTA announced a $14.1 million award in September 2026, but no source gives a construction schedule, so this is an expected target, not a schedule.

costs.what: Total project cost per SFCTA's April 2026 funding plan (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design); from SFCTA's April 2026 board packet as read on 2026-09-28, which could not be re-read in October 2026, so the figure is not re-checked
Prop L design-phase allocation, approved by the SFCTA Board

Federal Transit Administration All Stations Accessibility Program award announced for this project's ADA improvements (Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board); the announcement was in September 2026 (Trains.com, September 16: "last week"), and no grant agreement was read

facts.value: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), with funding from SFCTA (Prop L) and the FTA

One ramp on the northbound platform (about 305 ft long, 6.5% slope) and one on the southbound platform (about 465 ft long, 6.1% slope), plus tactile strips, lighting and signage. Platforms sit about 25 ft below street grade, currently reachable only by stairs.

open_questions: This record's placement under Pier 70 rather than Potrero Power Station reflects a roughly equal real-world distance (about 400-450m to each tracked boundary) plus the station's more established association with the Dogpatch/Pier 70 corridor in transit planning -- not a precise geometry test against a real station footprint (no Assessor parcel or site-plan figure exists to test against; the map shape is a coarse placeholder box; see its accuracy note).

No construction start date is confirmed in any source this record can currently cite; design is only at an early stage as of 2026-09-28. (An earlier spring 2028 target came from the April 14, 2026 board packet, which could not be re-read and was removed; see below.)

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the summary and the completion milestone no longer give a spring 2028 construction start, a mid/late 2029 completion or the $19,134,000 total, because the April 14, 2026 SFCTA board packet they came from refuses automated fetches and could not be re-read; they now follow SFCTA's readable April 28, 2026 post (design by summer 2027, construction funding sought to implement the project by June 2029). The $19,134,000 cost entry and its breakdown stay, marked as not re-checked until the packet can be re-read.
